spec=.claude/veriloop/specs/preroll-dev-cards-r1.md (RATIFIED, BINDING). Implement the R1 pre-roll dev-card window so the policy can learn it. This unblocks a retrain, so correctness matters far more than speed.

TDD IS BINDING: write the failing test FIRST and observe it fail against the current tree before implementing. Report each red-first result with its failure output.

SCOPE NOTE: spec D6 (opponent-side pre-roll via the heuristic) ALREADY LANDED with the bc-coverage-and-bank-legality slice — agents/heuristic.py now has a real dev-card policy including a pre-roll Knight. Do NOT redo it. Verify it is present and move on.

BUILD THESE (spec decisions):

D2 FIRST — HOIST THE TURN-BOUNDARY BOOKKEEPING. This is load-bearing and must precede opening the window. src/catan_rl/env/catan_env.py `_do_roll_for_agent` currently runs `agent.updateDevCards()` and `agent.devCardPlayedThisTurn = False` INSIDE the roll handler. Two bugs follow directly from opening a pre-roll window before it: (1) TWO DEV CARDS PER TURN — a pre-roll play sets the flag, the roll clears it, and the mask re-offers the card. This is reward-positive so PPO will find and exploit it within single-digit updates and every R1 number would measure a cheat. (2) a card bought on turn N is invisible at turn N+1's pre-roll node because updateDevCards() has not run yet, which ships a third ruleset, neither R0 nor Colonist. Move BOTH statements to the true turn boundary — every site that sets roll_pending = True for the agent. The opponent seat is ALREADY CORRECT (its refresh precedes rollDice()); insert its window after the refresh and leave that ordering alone. scripts/play_vs_model.py:373-377 is a working reference implementation including a comment naming this exact bug. src/catan_rl/bc/dataset.py has the identical ordering relative to its roll record and must move with it.

D3 — SHARE THE MASK HELPER; NEVER HAND-ROLL THE PRE-ROLL BRANCH. policy/heads.py masked_log_softmax returns UNIFORM for an all-zero mask, SILENTLY (its docstring says 'Rows with no valid entries return a uniform log-prob'). res1/res2 default keys are zero-initialised and set only inside the main-turn block. So a hand-rolled pre-roll branch that sets the four type bits but forgets the resource masks yields a pre-roll YoP granting two uniformly-random resources and a Monopoly monopolising a random one — valid indices, no crash, green suite, silently random play. Extract the existing main-turn dev-card legality block into a module-private helper that sets the type bits AND the resource masks, and call it from BOTH the pre-roll branch and the main-turn block. ROLL_DICE must be set FIRST so the `if not type_mask.any()` END_TURN fallback can never fire at a pre-roll node — pin that as a test. catan_env.py's roll branch must dispatch on an explicit WHITELIST of pre-roll dev types, keeping the existing no-op fallback for everything else.

D4 — EXCLUDE PLAY_ROAD_BUILDER FROM THE PRE-ROLL SET. Road Builder writes road_building_roads_left = 2 while roll_pending is still true, and the road-builder block sits BELOW the roll block in both env/masks.py and env/catan_env.py, so the two free roads would defer across the roll, a possible 7, discard and robber. The obvious fix is a trap: hoisting that block above the roll gate makes the road-builder branch's `if not edge_mask.any(): type_mask[END_TURN] = True` reachable pre-roll — the agent would END ITS TURN WITHOUT EVER ROLLING. Pre-roll Road Builder has ~zero tactical value (roads cannot interact with a dice roll). Include Knight, Monopoly and YoP; exclude Road Builder and say why in a comment.

D8 — MAKE THE RULESET A PER-ENV CONSTRUCTOR ARG, AND REFUSE CROSS-RULESET H2H. eval/cross_arch.py calls the LIVE compute_action_masks, so an R0 checkpoint would be silently evaluated under R1 rules, sampling from a region of its own type head that received exactly zero gradient. eval/harness.py `_run_matchup_games` takes a SINGLE SHARED env, so 'R0 policy under R0 rules vs R1 policy under R1 rules' is not expressible today. Thread a `ruleset` constructor arg through CatanEnv and EvalHarness. A cross-ruleset h2h must REFUSE, not annotate. This is a prerequisite for D9's accept-gate replacement, not a nicety.

D11 — ADD THE ONE-DEV-CARD-PER-TURN INVARIANT. eval/rules_invariants.py has six checks, ALL post-game state assertions; none tracks anything per-turn, so the suite structurally cannot see this bug class. Add 'at most one non-VP dev card per turn' (VP cards are never played and must not consume the allowance). run_all_invariants is already wired into eval/harness.py, search/eval_search.py, human_data/engine_bridge.py and scripts/play_vs_model.py, so one function earns coverage in all four for free. This is the highest value-per-line item in the slice — it is the tripwire that proves the retrain is measuring the real game rather than a bug it learned to exploit.

CONFORMANCE RECORDER (part of D10): src/catan_rl/conformance/recorder.py rolls unconditionally at every turn top, so all committed fixtures are 100% RollDice openers and re-recording under R1 yields byte-identical logs — the harness is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to this change class. Add a pre-roll _play_actions-style call between the turn-start refresh and the roll, and bump CONFORMANCE_SCHEMA_VERSION since within-turn step ordering changes. (The Torevan TypeScript half of D10 is handled separately by the main session; do not attempt to edit a sibling repo.)

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT touch src/catan_rl/engine/. PINNED_ENGINE_TREE must remain 261098d190c8. The `# TO-DO: Add option of AI Player playing a dev card prior to dice roll` at engine/game.py:522 lives inside playCatan(), the legacy pygame loop whose only caller is __main__ — the RL stack never enters it. Touching it turns make test-unit RED via the unconditional engine-parity test and retires the tree the accept-gate clause-(a) n=600 result was measured on. Leave it; the TODO remains an accurate description of playCatan.
- Do NOT build exploration machinery (spec D5 requires a MEASUREMENT first, which the main session will run after this lands).
- Do NOT regenerate the BC corpus and do NOT launch training.
- Both seats must end up with identical pre-roll legality — verify, do not assume.

ACCEPTANCE (beyond the gate): a pre-roll play followed by a roll leaves NO second dev card legal (must FAIL against the un-hoisted tree); a card bought turn N is playable at turn N+1's pre-roll node; pre-roll YoP/Monopoly expose the same resource masks as their main-phase counterparts; END_TURN is never legal at a pre-roll node and no BUILD_* type is; Road Builder excluded; agent and opponent seats symmetric; cross-ruleset h2h refuses; the one-dev-card invariant fires on a constructed violation.

implSummary:
Implemented spec `preroll-dev-cards-r1` (R1 pre-roll dev-card window) entirely inside `env/` + its consumers; no `src/catan_rl/engine/` edit and no PINNED_ENGINE_TREE re-pin.

NEW MODULE `src/catan_rl/env/ruleset.py` — `RULESET_R0`/`RULESET_R1`/`VALID_RULESETS`/`validate_ruleset` and `PRE_ROLL_DEV_TYPES = {PLAY_KNIGHT, PLAY_YOP, PLAY_MONOPOLY}`, with the D4 rationale for excluding `PLAY_ROAD_BUILDER` documented on the constant.

D3 (masks) — extracted the main-turn dev-card block into module-private `_set_dev_card_legality(...)`, which sets the type bits AND every resource default. Spec line refs were stale: the block had grown from `:204-217` to `:221-252` (the bank-legality slice added `resource1_yop`/`resource2_yop`/`resource2_yop_same`), so the helper carries the whole YoP bank triple, not just `res1_def`. `compute_action_masks` gained `*, ruleset: str = RULESET_R0` — a default-valued keyword, so every pre-existing call site is byte-identical; the pre-roll branch sets `ROLL_DICE` FIRST, then calls the helper with `allow_road_builder=False`, making the bottom-of-function `END_TURN` fallback structurally unreachable pre-roll.

D2 (the hoist, done first) — `updateDevCards()` + `devCardPlayedThisTurn = False` moved out of `_do_roll_for_agent` into a new `CatanEnv._begin_agent_turn()` called at all four agent `roll_pending = True` sites. Same hoist applied in `bc/dataset.py` (the two statements now sit ABOVE the `"roll"` `_record_decision`, which previously recorded a stale dev hand).

D2/D8 (env) — `CatanEnv.__init__(..., ruleset: str = RULESET_R1)`, validated and threaded into `_compute_masks`. `step`'s roll branch dispatches on the explicit `PRE_ROLL_DEV_TYPES` whitelist through the shared `_apply_main_action`, propagates only `robber_placement_pending`, asserts `road_building_roads_left == 0`, and leaves `roll_pending` True.

SEAT SYMMETRY (acceptance #8) — verified, not assumed: D6's heuristic `heuristic_pre_roll` was already present, but the SNAPSHOT opponent had no pre-roll path, so self-play would have run an R1 learner against a structurally-R0 opponent. New `CatanEnv._opponent_pre_roll()` samples the snapshot at its own `roll_pending` node, applies a whitelisted type, resolves a follow-on Knight robber, and is followed by a mirrored `victoryPoints >= maxPoints` guard (a pre-roll Knight can win via Largest Army). Branch order needed NO change — `robber_placement_pending` was already tested above `roll_pending` in both files.

D8 (eval) — `CrossArchEnv` forwards `ruleset`; `EvalHarness(..., ruleset=RULESET_R1)` builds both its envs with it; `evaluate_vs_policy` / `evaluate_policy_vs_policy` gained `opponent_ruleset` and RAISE the new `CrossRulesetEvalError` on mismatch (refuse, never annotate).

D11 — `check_one_dev_card_per_turn`, wired into `run_all_invariants` (so `eval/harness.py`, `search/eval_search.py`, `human_data/engine_bridge.py`, `play_vs_model.py` all get it free). Two mechanisms because `engine/broadcast.py` is out of scope and has no dev-card-played event: exact `DICE_ROLL`-segmented attribution of `YOP`/`MONOPOLY`, plus an aggregate pigeonhole over the cumulative counters (`plays <= rolled turns + 1`; the +1 slack is load-bearing).

D10 (Python half) — `conformance/recorder.py` gained `_pre_roll_actions` (same `rng`, whitelist-only) emitting a real pre-roll step before `RollDice`; `CONFORMANCE_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1 -> 2. No conformance fixtures are committed in this repo (`scripts/record_conformance.py` writes into the sibling Torevan checkout), so the bump breaks nothing here. THE TOREVAN TS HALF IS NOT IN THIS SLICE and remains owed.

R0 PINS — `scripts/play_vs_model.py` (`kwargs.setdefault("ruleset", RULESET_R0)` in `HumanVsBotEnv.__init__`, keeping its `"preroll": false` stamp and "both seats post-roll only" docstring TRUE), `bc/dataset.py` and `labeling/scenario_gen.py` pass `RULESET_R0` explicitly.

TDD, red-first VERIFIED by temporarily reverting the hoist and re-running: `test_preroll_play_then_roll_leaves_no_second_dev_card` and `test_card_bought_last_turn_is_playable_at_next_preroll` both FAIL on the un-hoisted tree (acceptance #2, #3), and `test_roll_rows_are_recorded_after_the_turn_boundary` fails on the old BC ordering. 25 new tests cover acceptance #2-#8 plus R0 preservation, the cross-ruleset refusal, the D11 invariant (including the +1-slack boundary), the schema bump, and a real pre-roll step appearing before a `RollDice` in a recorded fixture.

NOT DONE (spec non-goals / later stages, called out in the appended Implementation notes): D5's frozen-policy pre-roll histogram (acceptance #9), D7's BC regeneration, D9's accept-gate replacement, exploration machinery, any `engine/` edit, and the Torevan TS change. Acceptance #9 and the TS half of #11 are therefore still OPEN.

Docs sync per CLAUDE.md §6: new R0/R1 epoch section + ruleset-table row in `CLAUDE.md`, action-space note in `README.md`, and an "Implementation notes" appendix on the spec recording the stale line refs, the snapshot-symmetry work the spec did not enumerate, and that ALL banked numbers (v8 0.668 WR, search +54.6 Elo, accept-gate clause-(a) n=600) are R0-epoch and not comparable to R1.

Both have one-line fixes.

The code comment claims the tie to `audit_rules` avoids this tax ("with the audit off nothing reads the retained broadcast log ... so retaining it unread taxed the hottest operation in the search eval path"), but the tax is paid in the default configuration, not avoided. Measured in this worktree (`CatanEnv(ruleset=R1)` driven to a late-game state, 30 clones each): `audit_events=False` -> 0 events retained, `clone_env` = **1.99 ms**; `audit_events=True` -> 1053 events retained, `clone_env` = **5.10 ms** (2.6x). `clone_env` is called once per simulation expansion (`mcts.py:468`) plus once per determinization root (`mcts.py:329`), so at sims=100 this is roughly +0.3 s/move and +30 s/game, growing as the event log grows (~2.6k events in a full R1 game per the spec's own implementation notes). Not a correctness bug; the whole gate is green.
findings.fix: Detach the audit stream inside `clone_env` exactly as `_snapshot_opponent` is detached: before `copy.deepcopy(env)`, pop `env.game.broadcast.events` and remove the `_EventLog` subscriber from `broadcast._subscribers`; restore both in the `finally`. Simulated clones never read the audit stream, so they should not carry it. Then `audit_events=audit_rules` costs nothing and the comment becomes true.

findings.issue: `check_one_dev_card_per_turn` — the spec's "highest value-per-line item in the slice" and the tripwire that is supposed to prove the retrain measures the real game — does NOT catch a D2-class violation whose second card is ROAD BUILDER. Verified empirically against a simulated pre-hoist tree (the exact bug D2 fixes): pre-roll Monopoly, roll, main-phase Road Builder in the same turn produced `monopolyPlayed=1, roadBuilderPlayed=1` and `check_one_dev_card_per_turn` did NOT flag it. Mechanism 1 cannot attribute Road Builder (no event), and mechanism 2's deliberate `+1` slack absorbs a single straddle exactly (`total=2 <= turns+1=2`). The docstring says mechanism 2 is the "aggregate catch-all" for `ROADBUILDER`, which is only true beyond the slack — so the stated coverage overclaims. (The primary exploit, double Knight, IS caught: my probe against the same simulated pre-hoist tree got `FLAGGED -> player 'Agent' played 2 non-VP dev cards in one turn (... 2 Knight(s) inferred from 2 robber move(s)...)`.)
findings.fix: Restrict the `+1` slack to the only case that needs it. The slack exists solely because a pre-roll play can end the game before that turn's roll is emitted — which by construction only the WINNER can do. Change the aggregate bound to `allowed = turns + (1 if getattr(p, "victoryPoints", 0) >= getattr(game, "maxPoints", 15) else 0)`. That flags the probe case (`total=2 > turns=1`) while keeping the genuine game-ending-pre-roll case legal. `tests/unit/eval/test_preroll_eval.py:352 test_one_card_of_slack_is_allowed_for_a_game_ending_preroll_play` needs its stub player given winning VP, and a new regression test for the pre-roll+Road-Builder straddle should be added.

findings.issue: Seat asymmetry in mid-turn win detection, newly widened by this slice. The opponent seat got an explicit guard (`_run_opponent_turn`, catan_env.py:897-899: `if opp.victoryPoints >= self.game.maxPoints: return`) so a pre-roll Knight that wins via Largest Army stops the turn. The agent's pre-roll branch returns hardcoded `False, False`, so an agent pre-roll Knight that reaches 15 VP is not detected until END_TURN — the agent still places the robber and rolls the dice (possibly a 7, triggering an opponent discard and bank production) after having already won. The spec declares mid-turn win latency a non-goal ("pre-existing in kind, flagged not fixed"), and the winner is not misattributed (`_check_terminal` prefers the agent), so this is noted rather than blocking — but the two seats now behave differently at the same node.
findings.fix: Either mirror the opponent guard (`if agent.victoryPoints >= self.game.maxPoints: terminated, _ = self._check_terminal(); return self._get_obs(), self._terminal_reward(), terminated, False, self._terminal_info(terminated)`), or add one sentence to the pre-roll branch comment recording that the agent seat deliberately does NOT mirror `_run_opponent_turn`'s guard and why.

findings.issue: `assert ts.road_building_roads_left == 0` (also at catan_env.py:983 in `_opponent_pre_roll`) is a bare `assert` pinning the D4 exclusion — the load-bearing guarantee that no free-road sub-phase can straddle the roll. Bare asserts are stripped under `python -O`, and long training runs are launched via `nohup python scripts/train.py`, where a future whitelist edit would silently reintroduce the exact failure D4 exists to delete.
findings.fix: Either promote to a real check (`if ts.road_building_roads_left: raise AssertionError(...)`) or note in the comment that the pin is a debug-only assert and that `PRE_ROLL_DEV_TYPES` in `env/ruleset.py` is the real guarantee (it is already tested by `test_road_builder_excluded_preroll_but_legal_main_phase`).

findings.issue: Acceptance #2 and #3 pins are conditionally skipped. `test_preroll_play_then_roll_leaves_no_second_dev_card` wraps its whole "no second dev card is offered" assertion in `if not (env.discard_pending or env.robber_placement_pending):`, and `test_card_bought_last_turn_is_playable_at_next_preroll` early-`return`s when the opponent's roll produced a discard. Deterministic at seed 0 today (I confirmed both bodies do execute), but a dice/engine/seed change would silently turn the slice's two headline acceptance criteria into no-ops with a green suite — the same silent-pass failure mode this spec is built around.
findings.fix: Assert the branch actually taken before proceeding (e.g. `assert not env.discard_pending, "seed no longer reaches the intended state"`), so a drifting seed turns the test red instead of vacuous.

findings.issue: `checkpoint_ruleset` does a full `torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)` — unpickling the entire payload including optimizer state — to read one string, and it is called redundantly. `scripts/eval_cross_arch.py:126-128` loads BOTH checkpoints for the pre-run epoch print, then `cross_arch_h2h` (eval/cross_arch.py:285-292) loads both again. `scripts/elo_ladder.py:105` adds one extra full unpickle per matchup task in the parallel round-robin. Correct, just wasteful.
findings.fix: Memoize on the resolved path (`functools.lru_cache` over `str(Path(ckpt_path).resolve())`), or pass the already-resolved epoch down from `scripts/eval_cross_arch.py` instead of letting `cross_arch_h2h` re-derive it.

lenses.summary:
GO, with fixes. I ran the real gate in the worktree: `make typecheck` exit 0 (mypy, 150 files), `make lint` exit 0 (ruff), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` exit 0, `make test-unit` exit 0 (3109 passed / 6 skipped, 423s), `make check-env` exit 0. `git diff main -- src/catan_rl/engine/` is empty and `PINNED_ENGINE_TREE` is still `261098d190c88923639018b52f92f583a30d2081` (`test_engine_parity_holds_at_head PASSED`), so D1's scope discipline holds.

I verified the load-bearing claims rather than trusting them. Acceptance #2 is genuinely red-first: I re-ran it against a simulated un-hoisted tree (monkeypatched `_begin_agent_turn` back to a bare `roll_pending = True` and `updateDevCards()`/`devCardPlayedThisTurn = False` back inside `_do_roll_for_agent`) and got `flag after roll: False` / `PLAY_KNIGHT re-offered after the roll: True` — the two-dev-cards-per-turn exploit reproduces exactly as D2 predicted, and the shipped tree closes it. D2's hoist covers every agent-side site (`catan_env.py:510`, `:586`, `:797`, `:800`, plus `engine_bridge.rebuild_env`); no bare `roll_pending = True` survives, and the opponent's pre-existing refresh-before-roll ordering was left alone. D3's `_set_dev_card_legality` genuinely carries the full YoP bank triple (`res1_yop`/`res2_yop`/`res2_yop_same`) plus `res1_def`, not just the type bits — the silent-uniform trap is closed and pinned. D4 excludes Road Builder from `PRE_ROLL_DEV_TYPES` with the reasoning in the module. `ROLL_DICE` is set first and the pre-roll branch returns before the `END_TURN` fallback, so that fallback is structurally unreachable. D8 refuses on both seats and reads epochs off checkpoint stamps (the `cross_arch_h2h` new-seat regression test is a real one). D11's Knight-from-robber inference is sound: legitimate play tops out at one inferred knight (pre-roll Knight + own rolled 7 gives 2 robber moves minus the 7's entitlement), and the heuristic guards `devCardPlayedThisTurn` in `heuristic_pre_roll`/`_knight_is_useful`, so it cannot false-positive on the shipped opponent. `configs/ppo_default.yaml` is the only config that opts into R1 and `("rollout","ruleset")` is resume-critical — the `selfplay_v8_cont_resume.yaml` trap is closed. Docs sync (CLAUDE.md epoch section, README, spec implementation notes) is unusually complete.

The problems are all outside the spec's enumerated surface: a measured deepcopy regression in the search-eval path, one un-threaded eval surface (`search/sprt.py`), and the cross-repo Torevan schema-version debt. No BLOCKER.

findings.issue: `run_search_matchup` now sets `audit_events=audit_rules`, and `audit_rules` DEFAULTS to True — so the default search-eval path retains the broadcast stream, and `clone_env` deep-copies that growing list on every MCTS expansion. I measured it in the worktree (`copy.deepcopy(env)`, 20 reps, R1 heuristic game): 0 events = 2.02 ms, 500 = 4.40 ms, 1500 = 5.17 ms, 2600 = 7.40 ms — a 3.7x slowdown of the single hottest operation in search, and it grows monotonically WITHIN a game. `clone_env` is called once per expansion (`mcts.py:468`), so at `sims_per_move=100` that is ~0.20 s/decision of pure copying early-game rising to ~0.74 s/decision late-game. Before this slice the cost was zero because nothing retained events. This is worse than a slowdown: under `SearchConfig.time_budget_s` it silently buys fewer simulations late in the game than early, biasing the exact surface the banked +54.6 Elo rung was measured on — and the spec's own RISKS section already warns that a search deepening regression would pass the sims/s gate. The implementation notes reason only about the `audit_rules=False` case; the default case pays the tax.
findings.fix: Make the log un-copyable by simulations: give `_EventLog` in `src/catan_rl/env/event_log.py` a `__deepcopy__` returning a fresh empty `_EventLog`, and have `attach_event_log` publish the list through a property/holder so the clone's `broadcast.events` comes back empty rather than deep-copied. Alternatively strip `broadcast.events` (and the subscriber) inside `clone_env` around the existing `set_snapshot_opponent(None)` save/restore — simulations are throwaway and nothing audits them. Re-run the 2600-event benchmark to confirm it returns to ~2.0 ms.

findings.issue: `run_sprt_agents_vs_reference` builds `CatanEnv(opponent_type="snapshot", max_turns=max_turns)` with no `ruleset`, so it hard-pins R0 with no way to opt in and no refusal. This is the reusable pentanomial SPRT gate shipped by spec 008 — a decision surface that seats checkpoint-backed agents against a `SnapshotOpponent` and returns an accept/reject verdict. Run an R1 champion through it and you get precisely D8's stated failure: a policy sampled in a region of its type head that received zero gradient, scored under rules it was not trained for, with no `CrossRulesetEvalError`. The omission is inconsistent rather than principled — the implementer correctly threaded the epoch through `human_data/engine_bridge.py`, which D8 also did not enumerate, on exactly this reasoning. Same shape at lower stakes: `scripts/pregate0.py:331`, `scripts/opening_sweep.py:723`, and `src/catan_rl/replay/recorder_loop.py:910` (the last is arguably covered by the spec's replay non-goal, but it will record R0 games for an R1 checkpoint).
findings.fix: Add a `ruleset: str = RULESET_R0` (and optionally `opponent_ruleset`) parameter to `run_sprt_agents_vs_reference`, pass it into the `CatanEnv(...)` call, and have `scripts/dev/probe_oracle_sprt.py` resolve it via `eval.harness.checkpoint_ruleset(ckpt)` the way `scripts/elo_ladder.py` and `scripts/run_exploiter_gate.py` now do. At minimum, add the same one-line `checkpoint_ruleset` resolution at the `pregate0.py` / `opening_sweep.py` call sites so an R1 checkpoint cannot be silently R0-ruled.

findings.issue: The schema bump lands here while the reference oracle still pins the old value: `Torevan/packages/engine/src/conformance/conformance.test.ts` asserts `expect(log.schema_version).toBe(1)`. This repo commits no fixtures (`git ls-files src/catan_rl/conformance` returns only source), so `make test-unit` is structurally incapable of catching it — the oracle goes RED the first time ANY fixture is regenerated, R0 fixtures included, whose steps are otherwise identical to v1. Spec D10 explicitly requires the TS half to land in the SAME slice ("Spec 009 is the template: it changed both engines in one slice"), and the constitution names this reviewer the owner of parity/golden-file drift. The TS work was descoped by the orchestrator, so this is coordination debt rather than an implementation defect — but as merged, the slice leaves the two engines one `record_conformance.py` run away from a red oracle, and the untracked `scripts/record_conformance.py` in the owner's main checkout is exactly the thing that would trigger it.
findings.fix: Do not regenerate any conformance fixture until `expect(log.schema_version).toBe(1)` in `Torevan/packages/engine/src/conformance/conformance.test.ts` is bumped to `2` and the TS `actions.ts` pre-roll acceptance lands. The dependency is already recorded in the `CONFORMANCE_SCHEMA_VERSION` docstring and CLAUDE.md; carry it into the owner's merge checklist so it is not discovered by a red oracle.

findings.issue: The agent's pre-roll branch returns hardcoded `False, False` with no terminal check, while the opponent seat got an explicit `if opp.victoryPoints >= self.game.maxPoints: return` guard immediately after its window (`:897-899`). A pre-roll Knight that takes Largest Army at 13-14 VP wins on the spot, but the agent env then still resolves the robber and rolls the dice (possibly a 7, with discard and robber) before `_check_terminal` fires at the next main-phase action. I traced it: no outcome changes (the opponent gets no turn in between, `_turn_count` does not advance so truncation cannot intervene, and production grants no VP), so this is latency only — and the spec lists mid-turn win-detection latency as flagged-not-fixed. Noting it because it is a NEW third site of a class the spec enumerated as two, and because it is the one place the two seats' pre-roll handling differ.
findings.fix: Mirror the opponent guard: after the pre-roll `_apply_main_action` / `robber_placement_pending` write, call `terminated, truncated = self._check_terminal()` and return `self._terminal_reward()` / `self._terminal_info(terminated)` when it fires.

findings.issue: Both comments justify the D2 hoist partly by claiming the recorded roll row's obs "carried a stale dev hand: a card bought on turn N-1 was still in `newDevCards`" and therefore invisible to the obs. That half is false — `policy/obs_encoder.py:803-808` (`_dev_counts(hidden=True)`) and the opponent hidden-count path at `:722` both already fold `newDevCards` into the counts, so promotion is obs-neutral. The real and sufficient justification is the stale `devCardPlayedThisTurn` flag, which does gate the mask. Doc-truth drift in a comment that exists to explain a load-bearing reorder.
findings.fix: Drop the `newDevCards` clause from both comments and keep the `devCardPlayedThisTurn` justification. (The test's `n_new == 0` assertion is still a fine ordering pin — just relabel what it proves.)

findings.issue: `evaluate_vs_policy` compares `opponent_ruleset` against `self.ruleset` without running it through `validate_ruleset`. A typo (`"r1"`, `"R2"`) is treated as a cross-epoch mismatch and raises `CrossRulesetEvalError` naming an epoch that does not exist; with `allow_mixed_ruleset=True` it reaches `CatanEnv(opponent_ruleset=...)` which does raise `ValueError`. Fail-closed in both directions, so this is hygiene, not a hole — but the error message misleads. Every other epoch entry point in the slice validates.
findings.fix: `opponent_ruleset = None if opponent_ruleset is None else validate_ruleset(opponent_ruleset)` at the top of the method, matching `cross_arch_h2h` and `evaluate_search_vs_policy`.

findings.issue: `checkpoint_ruleset` does a full `torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)` — deserializing the entire policy state dict — to read one config string. It is now called once per matchup in `scripts/elo_ladder.run_match` (which fans out across cores), once per `evaluate_policy_vs_policy` on top of `build_actor`'s own load, twice in `cross_arch_h2h`, and three times in `expert_iteration/gate.run_gate`. Roughly doubles checkpoint I/O on the ladder path.
findings.fix: Optional. If the ladder wall-clock matters, memoize per path (`functools.lru_cache`) or hoist the resolution to the task-construction site in `scripts/elo_ladder.py` so each checkpoint is read once per process rather than once per matchup.

findings.issue: `assert ts.road_building_roads_left == 0` is the stated pin that no free-road sub-phase can straddle the roll, but bare `assert` statements are stripped under `python -O`. The whitelist in `env/ruleset.py` already makes the condition unreachable, so this is defence-in-depth rather than the primary guarantee — worth knowing if it is ever treated as the guarantee.
findings.fix: Either leave it (the whitelist plus `test_road_builder_excluded_preroll_but_legal_main_phase` are the real pins) or promote it to an explicit `raise RuntimeError(...)` if it is meant to survive optimized runs.

findings.issue: Spec acceptance #9 — the frozen-policy pre-roll type histogram recorded in a tracked file BEFORE any exploration knob — is not in this slice. The implementation notes correctly record it as owed and the orchestrator explicitly delegated it to the main session, so this is not an implementation gap. Flagging only so it is not lost: D5 makes that measurement the precondition for any exploration machinery, and the spec's own pre-mortem is about R1 shipping with nothing readable measured.
findings.fix: Track it as the next action after this branch lands: warm-start, widen the mask, freeze the policy, log the pre-roll type histogram over ~1k rollout steps into a tracked file, and only then decide on an exploration lever.
